subject: Physics
_transcription: Pages p16-p30 of the 2022 render, one question per page with options labelled A-D (p16 = Q1 under the heading 'Physics: Set A' ... p30 = Q15). The subject's own footers read Page 2-Page 15 on p17-p30 (p16 carries none). Numbers run 1-15 unbroken, no continuation or blank pages. Options kept in printed order. Q8's option graphs are laid out in a 2x2 grid (A top-left, C top-right, B bottom-left, D bottom-right); the optionFigures follow the labels A, B, C, D. Q14's option graphs are stacked A-D down the page. Spellings kept as printed: 'pullies' (Q7). Stem figures: Q4, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13. Picture options: Q8, Q14.

rows.text: A particle experiences an acceleration \(\vec{a} = \alpha \vec{v}\), where \(\vec{v}\) is the velocity of the particle and \(\alpha\) is a constant. If the distances traveled by the particle in the time intervals \(t_2 - t_1\) and \(t_3 - t_1\) are \(S_{12}\) and \(S_{13}\), respectively, which of the following relations is true?

A point mass \(m\) attached to a massless string is undergoing circular motion in a vertical plane. The length of the string is \(R\) and the acceleration due to gravity is \(g\). If the minimum value of the tension in the string is \(2mg\), the maximum speed of this circular motion of the point mass is

rows.subtopic: Common Forces in Mechanics and Friction
rows.text: An object is released from rest from the inner edge of a hemispherical bowl, and it falls under gravity. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the bowl is \(\mu\). If the object covers an angular displacement \(\theta\) with respect to the center of the hemisphere when it stops for the first time, which of the following expressions is correct?

As shown in the figure a block is resting on a frictionless floor and is attached to the free end of a spring. The right edge of the block in equilibrium is at a distance \(d\) from the wall. When the spring is compressed by a distance \(d/2\) and released, the time-period of the motion is \(T\). Similarly, when compressed by a distance \(2d\) and released, the time-period is \(T_0\). Considering elastic collision between the block and the wall, what is the value of the quantity \(T_0/T\)?

figure.note: A wall on the left with a horizontal spring attached to it; the spring's free end holds a grey block resting on the floor; a second wall on the right. A double-headed arrow labelled d marks the gap between the block's right edge and the right wall.

rows.text: A liquid of density \(\rho\) in a container weighs \(W\). A cubic block of side \(L\) and density \(\rho_b < \rho\) is pushed by a stick to completely submerge the block in the liquid without touching the bottom. If \(g\) is the acceleration due to the gravity and liquid displaced by the stick is negligible, what is the new weight of the container as registered by the weighing machine below?

figure.note: A container of liquid standing on a dial weighing machine; a vertical stick, with a downward arrow above it, pushes a cube so that it is fully under the liquid surface and clear of the container's bottom.

rows.text: A monoatomic ideal gas at pressure \(P\) and volume \(V\) is first adiabatically compressed to volume \(\frac{V}{8}\) and then is allowed to expand isothermally back to its original volume. What is the final pressure of the gas?

rows.subtopic: The Speed of a Travelling Wave
rows.text: A uniform taut string with two point charges \(q\) and \(-q\) attached to its ends passes over two massless pullies kept \(L\) distance apart as shown in the figure. If \(f\) is the fundamental frequency of the part of the string over pullies, which of the following statements is correct?

figure.note: Two vertical supports each holding a pulley; a string runs across the top of the two pulleys, the top span marked L between the pulleys. Below, the string's two ends come back inwards and carry point charges q (left) and -q (right), separated by a distance marked L/2.

rows.subtopic: Electrostatic Potential due to Charges and Dipoles
rows.text: Two uniformly charged concentric thin spherical shells of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) have charges \(+Q\) and \(-Q\), respectively. How does the electrostatic potential vary with distance from the center of the shells?
options: V constant from 0 to r1, then falling along a curve from r1 to zero at r2
V constant at a low level from 0 to r1, jumping up at r1 to a higher value, then falling along a curve to zero at r2
V constant from 0 to r1, then falling along a straight line to zero at r2
V zero from 0 to r1, jumping up at r1, then falling along a curve to zero at r2

figure.note: Two concentric circles: the inner one of radius r1 labelled +Q, the outer one of radius r2 labelled -Q, with radius arrows from the common centre marked r1 and r2.

rows.text: Consider a very long cylinder of radius \(a\) having a uniform positive charge density \(\rho\). A sphere of radius \(a\) has been carved out (see figure), leaving no charge in that region. The distance radially outward to the cylinder, as measured from the center of the sphere is \(x\). At what value of \(x\) will the electric field be maximum?

figure.note: Side view of a long grey cylinder labelled rho, with a white circular hole (the carved sphere) of radius a touching its top and bottom edges; from the sphere's centre an arrow points straight down, out of the cylinder, labelled x.

rows.text: In the given circuit, the box B either contains a capacitor, or an inductor or a resistor. The current \(I\) versus time \(t\) plots for three cases (\(a_1\), \(a_2\), \(a_3\)) are shown in figures. The switch \(S\) is closed at time \(t = 0\). Which of the following is correct?
options: \(a_1\) corresponds to a resistor, \(a_2\) corresponds to a capacitor, \(a_3\) corresponds to an inductor.
\(a_1\) corresponds to a resistor, \(a_2\) corresponds to an inductor, \(a_3\) corresponds to a capacitor.
\(a_1\) corresponds to an inductor, \(a_2\) corresponds to a resistor, \(a_3\) corresponds to a capacitor.
\(a_1\) corresponds to an inductor, \(a_2\) corresponds to a capacitor, \(a_3\) corresponds to a resistor.

figure.note: Top: a single series loop of a box labelled B, a resistor R, a cell, a switch S and an ammeter (circle marked A). Below: three I versus t graphs starting at t = 0: a1 is a horizontal line at a constant current; a2 starts at a high current and decays towards zero; a3 starts at zero and rises towards a constant value.

rows.text: In the given circuit each of the resistors is of \(1\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) resistance and each of the capacitors has \(4\ \mu\mathrm{F}\) capacitance. What is the charge in the capacitor between the points B and F?

figure.note: A circuit drawn on the edges of a cube with corners A, B, C, D (front face: A bottom-left, B top-left, C top-right, D bottom-right) and E, F, G, H (back face: E bottom-left, F top-left, G top-right, H bottom-right). A 5V cell lies on edge A-D. Resistors on edges A-B, B-C, E-F, F-G, C-G, E-H and D-H. Capacitors on edges B-F, A-E and C-D. Edge G-H is a plain wire.

rows.subtopic: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and by Lenses
rows.text: A thin lens made of material of refractive index \(n_l\) forms the image at the position \(I\) of a point object held at \(O\) on the central axis of the lens, as is shown in the ray diagram below. Consider that the refractive index of the medium is \(n_m\) and \(n_l > n_m\) for the figure given. Where does the image form when \(n_l < n_m\)?

figure.note: A biconvex lens labelled n_l in a medium labelled n_m. Points on the central axis, left to right: A, O, B, then the lens, then C, I, D. A ray from O goes up to the lens and is bent down to meet the axis at I.

rows.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
rows.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect and its Experimental Study
rows.text: The figures in the options show the photocurrent \(J\) of a photoelectric material versus the frequency \(f\) of an incident light beam. The light beam can have three different intensities \(I_1\), \(I_2\), \(I_3\), with \(I_3 > I_2 > I_1\). Which of the options is correct?
options: J is zero up to one threshold frequency shared by all three curves, then rises steeply to flat saturation levels; the highest level is labelled I3, the middle I2 and the lowest I1

Three parallel straight lines rising from the f-axis at different starting frequencies; the line starting at the lowest frequency is labelled I1, the next I2 and the one starting at the highest frequency I3
J is zero up to one threshold frequency shared by all three curves, then rises steeply to flat saturation levels; the highest level is labelled I1, the middle I2 and the lowest I3

Three parallel straight lines rising from the f-axis at different starting frequencies; the line starting at the lowest frequency is labelled I3, the next I2 and the one starting at the highest frequency I1

rows.text:
Consider that in a fission of a single Plutonium (\(\mathrm{Pu}^{239}\)) atom 207 MeV energy is released. Assuming all atoms of Plutonium undergo fission, which of the following options is the closest estimate of the amount of Plutonium required for a 20,000 units of TNT explosion?
(1 unit of TNT \(= 4.184 \times 10^{9}\) J, 1 eV \(= 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) J)
